CLINICAL DETAILS: 31M. 36 hours of periumbilical pain migrating to the right iliac fossa, anorexia, rebound tenderness. CRP 96. ?Appendicitis.

TECHNIQUE: CT abdomen and pelvis, portal venous phase, following intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:
The appendix is dilated, measuring 11 mm in diameter, with mural hyperenhancement and periappendiceal fat stranding. There is a 7 mm appendicolith at the base. No periappendiceal collection or extraluminal gas to suggest perforation. The remaining small bowel and colon are of normal calibre with no bowel wall thickening or inflammatory change.

The liver, gallbladder and biliary tree are unremarkable.

The pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable.

The kidneys are unremarkable with no hydronephrosis. The bladder is unremarkable.

No free intraperitoneal gas. Small volume of free fluid in the pelvis. No collection.

Several small reactive mesenteric lymph nodes in the right iliac fossa, the largest 8 mm in short axis. The abdominal aorta is of normal calibre.

The pelvic organs are unremarkable.

The lung bases are clear. No aggressive bone lesion.

CONCLUSION:
1. Acute appendicitis with an appendicolith at the base.
2. No CT features of perforation.
Recommend surgical review.
